extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent agents and attorneys), USPTO OED staff, and legal professionals interested in USPTO disciplinary standards
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and sanctions governing disciplinary actions against practitioners who represent clients before the USPTO, including specific Rule violations, probation reporting obligations, enforcement procedures, and remedial measures. Focused on conduct in patent prosecution (communication, diligence, abandonment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is a patent agent registered to practice before the Office and is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdiction over disciplinary matters is pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26. Registered practitioners are accountable to these regulations when representing clients before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(2)-(4) — Client consultation and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Must reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished; keep the client reasonably informed about the status of a matter; and promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of violations include failing to inform the client about Office Actions and Notices of Abandonment, failing to consult with the client about responding or reviving abandoned applications, and failing to respond to client requests about the applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §11.103 — Diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure examples: not notifying the client of Office Actions, not communicating about responding to Office Actions, allowing applications to become abandoned without client communication or consent, and failing to take steps to revive abandoned applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §11.804(d) — Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office considers failing to respond to Office Actions, allowing applications to become abandoned without the client's consent, and failing to take steps to revive abandoned applications as conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction imposed — public reprimand and 24-month probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be publicly reprimanded and serve a twenty-four (24) month probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent is permitted to practice before the USPTO in patent matters during probation unless probation is revoked and he is suspended or otherwise loses authority to practice. The sanction is part of a settlement resolving the disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation reporting requirements (annual reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the probationary period Respondent must submit a report to the OED Director every 12 months (12 months and 24 months) reporting specified information about any U.S. utility patent applications entrusted to Respondent that had Notices of Abandonment predicated on failure to timely and/or properly respond to Office communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required report content (items (1)–(8)): (1) Identify by application number each affected application; (2) State whether/how/when Respondent reported the Office communication to the client before abandonment; (3) Provide documentary evidence of reporting (e.g., correspondence); (4) State whether/how/when Respondent reported the Notice of Abandonment to the client; (5) State whether/how/when Respondent counseled the client about the abandonment and whether counseling occurred in adequate time to avoid abandonment; (6) Provide documentary evidence of reporting/counseling about the Notice of Abandonment; (7) For each application where counseling was not in adequate time, identify application number and client and explain why counseling did not occur in adequate time; (8) If none, affirmatively report that there are no such applications to report in that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement for noncompliance during probation — Order to Show Cause and potential suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with the Agreement, Final Order, or USPTO Rules, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend Respondent for up to twelve (12) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (A) Issue the Order to Show Cause; (B) send it to Respondent at the last address on record per 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a); (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond. If after response the OED Director still believes noncompliance occurred, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request suspension up to 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing and additional disciplinary actions permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the OED Director from seeking discipline for misconduct that formed the basis for an Order to Show Cause or from seeking discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 through 11.57 for misconduct before, during, or after probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking review of any action taken under the enforcement provisions does not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance such action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension compliance obligations (37 C.F.R. §11.58 and §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended during any portion of the probationary period, Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the OED Director must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These CFR sections set out practitioner obligations and OED responsibilities during suspension (e.g., notification, return of files), and are incorporated by reference in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and future use of the disciplinary record
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice of public reprimand and probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record of the disciplinary proceeding shall be considered in future matters: (1) when addressing further complaints or evidence of the same/similar conduct, and (2) in any further disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or to rebut statements by or on Respondent's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating/remedial measures recognized by the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures adopted by Respondent intended to prevent recurrence were considered in reaching settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of mitigating measures include: providing clients with the practitioner's cell phone number for accessibility; obtaining a new email program and service that stores incoming and outgoing messages on a backup server and includes calendar and tickler reminders; incorporating a new docketing and tracking system and a backup docketing procedure on a cell phone with notifications; and cooperating with OED during investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to seek reconsideration or review
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This waiver is part of the settlement and final disposition of the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No party is awarded costs against the other as part of this settlement.
